result_summary: Refuted. The kernel premise holds: every entry of K at |i - j| = 60 is exactly 0.0 for N = M = 300 and the widest non-zero offset is 54. The predicted saturation of the order gap does not occur: on 300-statement sequences with one block of 10 moved, the median shipped opw_gap grows +286.6% from displacement 5 to 50 and +190.5% from 60 to 200 in the shuffled arm, +315.1% and +188.7% in the document-order control, and 10 of 10 sequences grow >= 20% from 60 to 200. The row-group split of the shipped coupling shows why: a block moved by d positions shifts the d statements it passes over by 10 positions each, and the gap is linear in the d + 10 displaced statements (slope 0.5833 per displaced fraction, intercept 0.0063, R^2 0.999 in the shuffled arm). The 10 block rows cost 0.02023 at d = 10 and 0.02027 at d = 200 (+0.19%), so the block's own cost is constant from 10 positions on, well below the 54-position float64 support; the growth from 60 to 200 comes from the passed-over rows (0.11992 → 0.39295). The coupling stops matching a displaced statement to itself below 10 positions (own-statement mass 0.1227 at d = 5, at most 0.000258 from d = 10) because the kernel's position cost pen(8) = 1.6355 already exceeds the largest pooled ground cost 1.3356. The float64 underflow exists and is not the limit that shapes the reading
caveats: The registered 600-statement length was not run: the registered pool holds 372 unique statements. A single moved block cannot be displaced without shifting the d statements it passes over, so the registered design varies the count of displaced statements together with the distance; the bar is on the order gap and was applied literally. The numeric pattern of the prediction does appear on the block rows alone (+31.12% from 5 to 50, +0.01% from 60 to 200), with the constant part starting at 10 positions and not at 54, so that component does not support the float64 mechanism either. One block start per sequence, drawn from positions 0 to 90, forward moves only. Sequences are concatenations of pooled statements and short documents, not one long authored document, and A_moved holds the same statements as A (smd at most 0.000302), so a pair that also differs in content is not measured. The displacement at which the position cost exceeds the ground cost depends on the encoder's ground-cost scale (largest pooled ground cost 1.3356). The unmoved pair opw_gap(A, A) reads a median 0.00655 (shuffled) and 0.00995 (document order), not 0. Readings outside the registered grid (the d = 0 row, the row-group split, the structure_closeness column, the linear fit and the position-cost table) enter no bar. Two observations for the orchestrator, outside this hypothesis: structure_closeness of the shuffled median reads 0.9117 at d = 50 and 0.8987 at d = 60, below STRUCTURE_THRESHOLD 0.9; other notebooks under notebooks/experiments were re-executed by another process during this run and show as modified in git status, none by this executor. No timing is quoted
